label: r2c3
name: best + long-horizon credit
hypothesis: Same as r1c2 but with gamma 0.99 and gae_lambda 0.95. Ordering mistakes, such as filling a cell under an overhang too early, are made early but only cost the +1 exact-build bonus at DONE about 10 steps later. With gamma 0.95 and lambda 0.9 that signal is heavily discounted and biased. Longer credit should teach the network to avoid placements that block the design. Refuted if dev success is no higher than 0.887 or drops.
last_analysis: The x-mirror remap is what made the task learnable (0 → 0.75). The best results are r2c3 (0.888, seeds 0.889 and 0.887) and r1c2 (0.887). Both use 128 envs and ent_coef 0.02, and r2c3 also uses gamma 0.99 and lambda 0.95. Changes that gave more updates or more samples (2 or 3 epochs, 64 envs) raised the best single seed to 0.91, but often made one seed collapse to about 0.45. So the 2-seed mean is limited by instability, not by capacity. Spending compute on the network (a third conv, a per-layer head, a footprint conv) cut samples and scored lower. Dev IoU is about 0.985, so the remaining errors are a few wrong or out-of-order bricks. In this last round I keep the r2c3 network and try to stabilise training: more but smaller updates with a lower learning rate, longer rollouts so returns are cut off less often, and per-pixel LayerNorm in the trunk.
